title: KB5138318 hotpatch fixes Server 2025 IPv6 route crash
summary: Microsoft released out-of-band hotpatch KB5138318 (OS build 26100.33732) on 25 November 2026 for Windows Server 2025 Datacenter: Azure Edition. It fixes a regression from the November hotpatch KB5131077: servers with Router Advertisement enabled that receive time-bound IPv6 routes could stop with error 0x139 (KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE) when a route timer expired. The fix applies without a restart, needs baseline KB5126646 and servicing stack 26100.33634 or later, and comes through Windows Update, WSUS and the Update Catalog.
why: An unplanned bugcheck on a hotpatched server defeats the point of hotpatching. The trigger is a normal IPv6 feature, so servers on networks that send route information in Router Advertisements are exposed even if nobody configured IPv6 on purpose.
todo: Find hotpatch-enrolled Windows Server 2025 machines that have KB5131077 and check System logs for unexpected 0x139 bugchecks since mid-November.
Deploy KB5138318; confirm baseline KB5126646 and SSU 26100.33634 or later first (`DISM /Online /Get-Packages | findstr /i ServicingStack`).
Microsoft's KB lists only Datacenter: Azure Edition; if you hotpatch Arc-connected Standard/Datacenter servers, confirm in Windows Update that the fix is offered to them too.
effective_note: Out-of-band hotpatch released 25 Nov 2026; no restart required. No known issues listed at publication.
